context.body: The LORD also will save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of David’s house and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem not be magnified above Judah.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

context.body: Royal, Poetic, and Prophetic Memory · Zechariah 12:7–14
context.label: Canonical location

observations.body: Judah’s tents are saved first, Jerusalem is defended, David’s house is compared to God’s messenger, a spirit of grace and supplication is poured out, and families mourn separately.
observations.label: David’s house is strengthened and then mourns: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps Judah, Jerusalem, David’s house, inhabitants, the pierced one, families, and the LORD, Judah’s tents, Jerusalem, and the land’s households, saving, defending, strengthening, seeking destruction, pouring a spirit, looking, and mourning visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: David’s house is strengthened and then mourns: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: Judah, Jerusalem, David’s house, inhabitants, the pierced one, families, and the LORD · Judah’s tents, Jerusalem, and the land’s households · saving, defending, strengthening, seeking destruction, pouring a spirit, looking, and mourning · exaltation language gives way to piercing and widespread differentiated grief
observations.label: Relationships named in Zechariah 12:7–14

payload.posture: Read Zechariah 12:7–14 as its own royal, poetic, and prophetic memory David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places exaltation language gives way to piercing and widespread differentiated grief inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
payload.title: David’s house is strengthened and then mourns
